name: Portable X-ray: preventive maintenance and quality control
description:
Yearly preventive maintenance and quality control for a mobile (portable) X-ray unit with a digital detector.

A starting point: check every limit against the manufacturer's service manual and your state's radiation control regulations, then add the manufacturers and models it is for.
reference: 21 CFR 1020.30–1020.31; IEC 62353; the manufacturer's service manual

steps.text: Before you start
Wear your dosimeter. Make test exposures only with the room cleared, standing at the full length of the exposure switch cord, behind a protective barrier or wearing a lead apron.
Photo of the dataplate (model and serial number)
steps.help: Take it with your phone or tablet; it is added to this work order.

steps.text: What powers the drive and generator?
Look it over
Housing, covers and warning labels are intact and readable
Tube head, collimator and arm: no cracks, dents or oil leaks
steps.help: An oil leak or cracked tube housing means the unit must not be used.

steps.text: Power and high-voltage cables: no cuts, kinks or exposed conductors
The arm and tube head stay where they are set, without drifting
Moving the unit
Wheels and casters roll freely; the parking brake holds the unit on a slope
Drive works forward and back; the unit stops as soon as the drive handle switch is let go
The unit stops when the collision bumper is pressed
Emergency stop cuts power to the drive and to exposures
Exposure switch: two-stage, works only while held, on a cord at least 2 m long
steps.help: 21 CFR 1020.31(i) asks for at least 1.8 m (6 ft) of cord for mobile units.

steps.text: Battery and charging
Battery voltage, fully charged
steps.help: Compare with the value in the manufacturer's service manual.

steps.text: Charger and charge indicator
Battery pack: next replacement due
Collimator and light field
Collimator light comes on and is bright enough to see in a lit room
Light field to X-ray field: total edge misalignment at 100 cm
steps.help: The light and X-ray field edges may differ by at most 2% of the distance (2 cm at 100 cm) along each axis (21 CFR 1020.31(d)).

steps.text: Generator performance (with a calibrated X-ray analyser)
Write the analyser's serial number and calibration due date in the note of the first reading.
kVp at 60 kV set
steps.help: Typical acceptance ±5% of the setting; use the manufacturer's tolerance if it is tighter.

steps.text: kVp at 80 kV set
kVp at 100 kV set
Exposure time at 100 ms set
Output reproducibility: coefficient of variation of 5 exposures
steps.help: Same settings, five exposures; CV = standard deviation ÷ mean output. Limit 0.05 (21 CFR 1020.31(b)).

steps.text: mAs linearity: difference between adjacent mAs stations
steps.help: |X1 − X2| ≤ 0.10 × (X1 + X2), where X is output per mAs (21 CFR 1020.31(c)).

steps.text: Half-value layer at 80 kVp
steps.help: At least 2.9 mm of aluminium at 80 kVp for equipment made after June 2006 (21 CFR 1020.30(m), table 1). Check the limit for older equipment.

steps.text: Image receptor
Detector calibration (gain and offset, or flat-field)
Detector housing, handle and battery undamaged; no drop alarm
QC phantom image: no artefacts, lines or dead areas
steps.help: Use the unit's own QC phantom and protocol.

steps.text: Photo of the phantom image or the QC result screen
Wireless detector pairs, and images arrive at the console
Electrical safety (IEC 62353)
Protective earth resistance, including the power cord
Equipment leakage current (direct or differential method)
steps.help: Limit for Class I equipment: 500 µA (1000 µA with the alternative method).

steps.text: Finishing
Lead aprons and thyroid collars kept with the unit are present and undamaged
Parts replaced
Overall result
Remarks
